answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation Form 8-K current report dated August 17, 2026 (SEC EDGAR), covering the SB Energy residual value guaranties for the Portsmouth Site

findings.claim: On August 17, 2026 NVIDIA entered multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy as Lessor for leases totaling about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site (Pike County, Ohio). Each Agreement generally becomes effective when its lease commences. NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation is capped at $105 billion for its initial commitment, and payments are conditional on the Lessor satisfying ready-for-service conditions, expected beginning in 2028.
findings.use: Supports a reading that NVIDIA has an existing, signed contingent financial obligation of up to $105 billion for the initial 4.25 GW commitment, with cash exposure deferred until lease commencement and ready-for-service, expected from 2028. It does not show that any payment will be made.
findings.grounds: The company is the direct party to the agreements and states their existence, date, counterparty, capacity and cap, so it can establish the existence and cap of the obligation. The Item 2.03 incorporation confirms it is treated as a direct financial or off-balance-sheet obligation. The uncertainty that matters is timing and trigger, not existence: the 2028 ready-for-service date is an expectation, and the cap is an upper bound, not an estimate of expected payments.
findings.next_check: The full Agreements, filed as an exhibit to the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, should show the guaranteed minimum values, payment schedule, lease commencement mechanics and how the $105 billion cap applies across leases. Later filings should show when leases commence and whether ready-for-service conditions are met.

findings.claim: The guaranty pays if the tenant, OpenAI (an affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC), suffers an insolvency that causes a lease default, or fails to make lease payments. NVIDIA then pays the shortfall between the guaranteed minimum lease value and amounts recovered through a replacement lease or sale. OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for amounts actually paid.
findings.use: Supports a conditional scenario in which NVIDIA's exposure depends on OpenAI's credit. NVIDIA's net loss is limited by the reimbursement only to the extent OpenAI's own credit can pay it. The source does not establish OpenAI's financial condition or the reimbursement's practical value.
findings.grounds: The trigger events and reimbursement promise are stated by NVIDIA as contract terms, so they are the company's own description of the agreement. They are not independently verified. The key uncertainty is OpenAI's ability to pay lease obligations and reimburse NVIDIA. The article gives no OpenAI financial data, so the reimbursement's value cannot be judged from this source.
findings.next_check: Review OpenAI's financial disclosures or credit assessments, the exhibit's definitions of insolvency and payment default, and the replacement-lease and sale recovery mechanics. Evidence that OpenAI's credit quality is weak, or that recoveries would fall well short of guaranteed minimums, would strengthen the risk scenario.

findings.claim: Upon a Trigger Event NVIDIA may assume the lease, require the Lessor to relet the premises, start a sale process, let the lease terminate, or defer these remedies for up to one year while paying specified project costs. The obligations end at the earliest of the 20th anniversary of lease commencement, lease termination by OpenAI under its terms, OpenAI reaching a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary events.
findings.use: Supports reading NVIDIA's guaranty as having several exit and remedy paths, and as tied to OpenAI's credit rating as a termination condition. Those paths could limit the obligation's duration, but the duration and conditions are not quantified in the source.
findings.grounds: These are the company's description of contract remedies and termination events. The company knows the terms it signed. What is unknown is the threshold for 'satisfactory credit rating', the cost of deferral, and how likely each remedy is to be used.
findings.next_check: The exhibit should define the satisfactory credit rating threshold, the project-cost obligations during the one-year deferral, and the 20-year term mechanics. Subsequent disclosure of any Trigger Event or remedy election would show which path is actually used.

findings.claim: NVIDIA can provide credit support for about an additional 3.8 GW at the Portsmouth Site, exercisable in its sole discretion.
findings.use: Leads to a question about possible further expansion of NVIDIA's guaranteed exposure, but the source does not show that this support will be provided, when, or on what terms. It is an option, not a committed obligation.
findings.grounds: The company states the option in its own filing, so the existence of the discretionary capacity is established. Whether NVIDIA will use it depends on management's future decision, which the source does not disclose. The company's expansion plans and the conditions for additional support are unresolved.
findings.next_check: Watch for any later agreement, 8-K or 10-Q disclosure exercising the 3.8 GW credit support, and any stated cap or terms that would apply to it.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says it has secured land, power and shell capacity at the Portsmouth Site to host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure through the partnership and the credit support. OpenAI, as tenant, will use capacity supporting about 4.25 GW of IT load to deploy NVIDIA's full-stack DSX AI factory platform, subject to limited exceptions.
findings.use: Supports the company's account of an announced commercial model in which NVIDIA's guaranty backs a site that the named tenant plans to use for NVIDIA's platform. This is a stated intention and a company characterization, not a confirmed deployment or revenue stream.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is the speaker and states the plan, so it knows its intended arrangement, but the claim about OpenAI's deployment is a statement of intent. The 'limited exceptions' are unspecified. The uncertainty that matters is whether the site is built and ready for service, and whether OpenAI actually deploys the platform.
findings.next_check: Evidence that the lease is signed, that construction is on schedule for the expected 2028 ready-for-service date, and that OpenAI's deployment of NVIDIA's DSX platform is occurring, would strengthen the deployment scenario. Evidence of delays or a different tenant would weaken it.

findings.claim: Forward-looking statement safe-harbor language, the furnished status of the Item 7.01 press release under Section 18, and the 10-Q reference for the full agreement are administrative disclosure text.
findings.use: No research use. The administrative footer adds no business evidence beyond what the substantive findings already use.
findings.grounds: This material is legal and procedural wording, not a claim about the business. It is useful only to note that the full terms are filed later and that the press release is not a filed document.
